reason: E2 shows that aging a eutectic HEA increased yield strength via nano-scale L12 precipitates, supporting the strength premise, but it does not address strain hardening, adiabatic shear band delay, or improved ductility under dynamic loading. E1 states that precipitation in H/MEAs typically causes strain localization and a 10–20% ductility reduction, directly contradicting the premises of enhanced uniform deformability and fracture strain. No evidence is provided that the specific HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy can form such precipitates or that they would improve dynamic properties.
premises: Nano-scale precipitates can be introduced in refractory HEAs via aging to increase strength.
Precipitation strengthening impedes dislocation motion and increases strain hardening.
Increased strain hardening delays adiabatic shear band formation under dynamic loading.
The HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy system can form beneficial nano-scale precipitates upon aging.
Aging-induced precipitates improve uniform deformability and fracture strain in HEAs.
